title: OOM Sentinel: per-request memory tickets, soft-reset circuit, and staged fallback chain
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem:
Large sustained continuous-batching workloads plus heavy KV cache pressure occasionally drive GPUs into unrecoverable OOMs. Current mitigation (hard eviction + broad model fallbacks) causes noisy degradation and long recovery windows. We need a coordinated per-request memory admission and a graceful, observable recovery mechanism that minimizes customer error rates and wasted compute while restoring healthy state quickly.

Proposal summary:
1) Memory tickets: allocate a per-request ephemeral ticket from a per-device memory pool that accounts for KV residency, anticipated KV growth (prefix/token heuristics), and worst-case activation memory. Tickets reserve headroom and are checked before admission to batching queues.
2) Soft-reset circuit: on persistent low-free-memory signals (configurable window), trigger a soft-reset path on a subset of workers: drain new requests, progressively trim large KV entries, snapshot hot prefixes to disk where feasible, and restart the local runtime with preserved minimal KV shards (staged warm rehydration). This is cheaper than full restart and preserves useful cache.
3) Staged fallback chain: instead of a single fallback model, implement a prioritized chain based on token-cost and semantic fidelity. On memory pressure or failed ticket allocation, route to the next model in the chain with parameterized hallucination/quality knobs and backoff retry windows.
4) Retry heuristics: failed or degraded responses are retried with an exponential backoff and ticket-bump policy that increases memory allocation only when upstream conditions (eviction progress or circuit cool-down) indicate safety.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (2 sprints): implement memory tickets and admission hooks in continuous-batcher; expose metrics (tickets_acquired, tickets_failed, ticket_wait_ms). Add config for heuristic ticket sizing (prefix-length, batch-size, kv-residency-estimate).
- Phase 2 (2 sprints): soft-reset circuit prototype: drain/trim workflow with per-worker safe checkpoints, background KV snapshot to fast storage, and restart path that rehydrates only hot-key set. Add tracing and SLO dashboards.
- Phase 3 (2 sprints): staged fallback chain + retry controller integrated into routing layer. Provide per-customer policy to prefer lower-latency downgrade vs higher-fidelity fallback.

Operational concerns and trade-offs:
- Ticketing adds admission latency when requests queue for tickets; mitigate with optimistic prefetch for warm sessions.
- Soft-reset requires fast persistent backing (NVMe) to make snapshots feasible; fall back to full eviction if absent.
- Fallback chain increases variance in user quality; require strict eval sets and rollout gating.

Metrics to monitor:
- OOM incidents per-device (target: reduce by 80% vs baseline)
- Mean time to healthy (recover to steady memory)
- Tickets_failed ratio and ticket_wait latency
- Customer error-rate and quality-regression on fallback routes

Rollout plan:
- Canary 5% of traffic on non-critical models; run for 72h with kill-switch. Gradual ramp to 100% with rollback criteria tied to OOMs and quality regressions.

Notes:
- Design doc and implementation details in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/oom-sentinel-design
- Prototype PRs will be opened under github.com/redwood-inference/runtime (WIP)
acceptance_criteria: Memory ticket admission integrated into continuous-batcher and covered by unit/integration tests
Soft-reset circuit can be triggered via feature flag and performs staged KV trim + rehydrate without full model reload
Fallback chain routing respects per-customer policy and records quality metrics per-tier
Canary run shows >=80% reduction in recoverable OOM incidents and no high-severity quality regressions
